name: Chip supply
summary: Nexperia and STMicro warn AI demand is squeezing mature-chip supply for carmakers; no TSMC or Samsung stoppage
state: At the Electronica fair in Munich on 9–10 Nov, Nexperia's interim chief executive said the company was 'totally oversubscribed' and STMicroelectronics' chief executive said he saw 'many bottlenecks', as suppliers shift capacity towards AI data centres and away from mature chips used in cars and industrial equipment (The Star, 10 Nov; BusinessDay, 11 Nov). Searches on 15 Nov found no TSMC or Samsung stoppage and no new controls halting a major supply chain, so reported shortages in a key segment keep this at Watch.
for_you: Tight supply of older-generation chips tends to show up first as longer lead times for cars, appliances and industrial equipment rather than empty shelves.
rubric_hit: Watch: shortages reported in a key segment (mature automotive chips, 9–10 Nov); no TSMC/Samsung disruption

sources.title: The Star — Chipmakers warn AI demand is creating bottlenecks in automotive supply chain
BusinessDay — AI chip demand creates bottlenecks in car supply chain

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
